module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 862

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/862](https://www.erdosproblems.com/862)
- [Er92c] Erdős, P., *Some of my forgotten problems in number theory*. Hardy-Ramanujan J. (1992),
  34-50.
- [SaTh15] Saxton, David and Thomason, Andrew, *Hypergraph containers*. Invent. Math. (2015),
  925-992.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Finset Filter

namespace Erdos862

/--
$A_1(N)$, the number of maximal Sidon subsets of $\{1, \dots, N\}$.
-/
noncomputable def numMaximalSidonSets (N : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  {A : Finset ℕ | A ⊆ Icc 1 N ∧ Set.IsMaximalSidonSetIn (A : Set ℕ) N}.ncard

/--
Let $A_1(N)$ be the number of maximal Sidon subsets of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$. Is it true that
$$A_1(N) < 2^{o(N^{1/2})}?$$

A problem of Cameron and Erdős. This is resolved as a consequence of results of Saxton and
Thomason [SaTh15] - they prove that the number of Sidon sets in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ is at least
$2^{(1.16+o(1))N^{1/2}}$. Since each Sidon set is contained in a maximal Sidon set, and each
maximal Sidon set contains at most $2^{(1+o(1))N^{1/2}}$ Sidon sets, it follows that
$$A_1(N) \geq 2^{(0.16+o(1))N^{1/2}}.$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos862.lean"]
theorem erdos_862.parts.i : answer(False) ↔
    (fun N : ℕ => Real.logb 2 (numMaximalSidonSets N : ℝ)) =o[atTop]
      (fun N : ℕ => (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/--
Let $A_1(N)$ be the number of maximal Sidon subsets of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$. Is it true that
$$A_1(N) > 2^{N^c}$$
for some constant $c>0$?

A problem of Cameron and Erdős. This is resolved as a consequence of results of Saxton and
Thomason [SaTh15] - they prove that the number of Sidon sets in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ is at least
$2^{(1.16+o(1))N^{1/2}}$. Since each Sidon set is contained in a maximal Sidon set, and each
maximal Sidon set contains at most $2^{(1+o(1))N^{1/2}}$ Sidon sets, it follows that
$$A_1(N) \geq 2^{(0.16+o(1))N^{1/2}}.$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos862.lean"]
theorem erdos_862.parts.ii : answer(True) ↔
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop,
      (2 : ℝ) ^ ((N : ℝ) ^ c) < (numMaximalSidonSets N : ℝ) := by
  sorry

/--
This is resolved as a consequence of results of Saxton and Thomason [SaTh15] - they prove that
the number of Sidon sets in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ is at least $2^{(1.16+o(1))N^{1/2}}$. Since each
Sidon set is contained in a maximal Sidon set, and each maximal Sidon set contains at most
$2^{(1+o(1))N^{1/2}}$ Sidon sets, it follows that
$$A_1(N) \geq 2^{(0.16+o(1))N^{1/2}}.$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_862.variants.lower_bound (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop,
      (2 : ℝ) ^ (((0.16 : ℝ) - ε) * (N : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)) ≤ (numMaximalSidonSets N : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos862

reformulations.difference: The source asks for sub-square-root exponential growth, expressed in Erdős's equation (15) by A₁(N) < 2^(ε√N) for every ε > 0 asymptotically. Lean instead tests whether log₂ A₁(N) = o(√N).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The counting family is finite and nonempty, so A₁(N) ≥ 1 and log₂ A₁(N) is nonnegative. Monotonicity of exponentiation converts the logarithmic little-o condition into the eventual exponential bound for every positive ε; using ε/2 supplies the strict inequality. Proved this equivalence for the actual counting function as Review862.upper_formulation_iff. The fixed answer(False) correctly records the negative resolution.

reformulations.difference: The source-derived bound A₁(N) ≥ 2^((0.16 + o(1))√N) is expressed as an eventual lower bound with coefficient 0.16 − ε, for each ε > 0.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: An error sequence tending to zero gives every ε-bound eventually. Conversely, the ε-bounds imply that r(N) = min(log₂(A₁(N))/√N − 0.16, 0) tends to zero, and this sequence supplies the source-form lower bound for positive N. Proved the equivalence, including existence of the error sequence, as Review862.lower_formulation_iff.

sources_consulted: Erdős, P., Some of my forgotten problems in number theory, Hardy–Ramanujan Journal 15 (1992), 34–50, §2, especially p. 39, equations (15)–(16): https://hrj.episciences.org/125/pdf

Saxton–Thomason, Hypergraph containers, arXiv:1204.6595v3, Theorem 2.11 and preceding Sidon-set definition and extremal bound. Read the abstract, LaTeX source, and HTML: https://arxiv.org/abs/1204.6595 ; https://arxiv.org/e-print/1204.6595 ; https://arxiv.org/html/1204.6595v3
FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/Basic.lean: IsSidon, Set.IsMaximalSidonSetIn, and their supporting lemmas.
review.notes:
No mathematical defects found in the definition or any of the three theorems. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles successfully and proves finiteness, positivity, agreement with a finite enumeration, inclusion-maximality equivalence, and both asymptotic reformulations without sorry. Counts for N = 0 through 10 are 1, 1, 1, 3, 3, 6, 14, 20, 24, 36, 64; neither ncard's infinite-set default nor logb's zero-input default is reached.

The solved tags and False/True answers agree with the cited published results. The linked proof's translated interval, natural logarithm, and non-strict lower bounds imply the repository statements. Its source contains no sorry or custom axiom declarations, but the external Lean 4.29.1 project was not rebuilt.

The live erdosproblems.com page remained blocked by Cloudflare despite descriptive User-Agent headers, so its newest commentary/status was not independently retrieved. The posed questions were checked directly against Erdős's original paper, and their resolution against Saxton–Thomason.
